## Safety picture for Lutathera (lutetium Lu-177 dotatate): focus on MDS and renal impairment (tool-integrated)

### Ground-truth FDA label (what’s explicitly warned/precautioned)
The FDA label (Warnings & Precautions) explicitly calls out all of the following as key safety issues for LUTATHERA: **myelosuppression** (with monitoring and dose modification guidance), **secondary myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) and leukemia** (with median time-to-onset values), and **renal toxicity** (hydration/urination guidance, creatinine/CrCl monitoring, and dose modification guidance).[^1^]  
The label also provides context that in NETTER-1, myelosuppression occurred more frequently in the LUTATHERA arm and gives detailed rates for anemia, thrombocytopenia, and neutropenia, as well as platelet nadir/recovery timing.[^1^]  
No boxed warning is present in the openFDA label record for LUTATHERA.[^2^]

### FAERS disproportionality (PRR) — main reported reactions
Below are the PRR values returned by the skill’s FAERS disproportionality calculations for LUTATHERA. **PRR is a reporting signal, not causality** (subject to confounding, stimulated reporting, and oncology indication/disease-course terms appearing as “reactions”).[^3^]

#### Important caveat on “indication terms”
Two of the highest-PRR terms—**NEUROENDOCRINE TUMOUR** and **METASTASES TO LIVER**—are very likely reflecting the treated disease/setting being reported in case narratives rather than drug toxicity signals; they should **not** be interpreted as adverse drug reactions.

### The two requested AEs in depth

#### 1) Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS)
**Label context:** Secondary MDS and leukemia are explicitly described in Warnings & Precautions. The label states median time to onset: **MDS 29 months** and **acute leukemia 55 months**, and provides incidence examples (NETTER-1 and ERASMUS).[^1^]  
**FAERS PRR:** “myelodysplastic syndrome” shows **PRR 7.524** in the tool output (strong disproportionality signal by the skill’s criteria).[^6^]  
**Literature context (tool-found):** The skill’s PubMed “reaction-linked” search (using LUTATHERA + the reaction term) returned **no matches** for “Lutathera” + “myelodysplastic syndrome” under that exact query constraint.[^18^]  
**Web-only context (supplement, not a finding):** A case report describing Lutetium-177 dotatate–associated hemolytic anemia with subsequent MDS features is surfaced via web search (DOI: 10.7759/cureus.22392).[^19^]

#### 2) Renal impairment / renal toxicity
**Label context:** Renal toxicity is explicitly described, including amino acid renal protection, hydration/urination advice, and monitoring of serum creatinine and calculated creatinine clearance; it notes patients with baseline renal impairment may be at increased risk.[^1^] The label adverse reactions table also includes “Renal failure” and “Creatinine increased” among reported adverse reactions/lab abnormalities.[^10^]  
**FAERS PRR:** “renal impairment” shows **PRR 2.289** (moderate disproportionality signal by the skill’s criteria).[^8^]  
**Literature context (tool-found):** The skill’s PubMed “reaction-linked” search returned **no matches** for “Lutathera” + “renal impairment” under that exact query constraint.[^20^]  
**Preclinical internal-doc context (Squirro):** A preclinical tolerability paper comparing terbium-161 vs lutetium-177 somatostatin analogues reported **minimal kidney abnormalities** on histology in treated mice, and notes kidney absorbed doses within a “reasonable range” for DOTATATE in that study’s conditions.[^21^][^22^] (Preclinical only; transferability to humans is explicitly caveated in the same document.)[^23^]  
**Web-only context (supplement, not a finding):** A J Nucl Med paper on 177Lu-DOTATATE PRRT in CKD stage 3 patients is surfaced via web search (DOI: 10.2967/jnumed.121.263056).[^24^]

### Myelosuppression / platelet effects (bridging label + FAERS + literature)
- **Label**: Myelosuppression is emphasized with monitoring and dose modification guidance; NETTER-1 rates for anemia/thrombocytopenia/neutropenia are explicitly summarized in Warnings & Precautions.[^1^]  
- **FAERS**: “PLATELET COUNT DECREASED” shows **PRR 7.946**[^5^] and “THROMBOCYTOPENIA” **PRR 3.918**[^7^], consistent with this being a key safety domain.  
- **Literature (tool-found, reaction-linked)**: For “THROMBOCYTOPENIA”, the skill retrieved multiple PubMed-indexed papers, including a FAERS-based postmarketing safety surveillance analysis and a hematotoxicity comparison study (Lutathera vs locally manufactured 177Lu-HA-DOTATATE; also assesses renal parameters), plus a phase I Lutathera+nivolumab trial where common TRAEs included lymphopenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia, and nausea.[^25^]

### Pharmacogenomic context
- **CPIC**: No CPIC guideline matched when filtering for “Lutathera” (empty result is normal and is itself the finding).[^26^]  
- **FDA pharmacogenomic biomarkers tool call**: The skill’s FDA PGx biomarker retrieval failed due to an FDA “apology/abuse-detection” page response (404), so **no FDA PGx biomarker context could be retrieved in this run**.[^27^]

### Trial context (ClinicalTrials.gov; skill-selected “has results” + Phase 2/3/4 filter)
The skill surfaced 8 trials (with results and Phase 2/3/4 filter applied in its query), including:
- **NETTER-1**: NCT01578239[^28^]  
- **NETTER-2**: NCT03972488[^29^]  
- A Phase 4 post-authorization safety study related to amino-acid solution (LysaKare): NCT04524442[^30^]  
(Additional trials listed in the skill output are available if you want them expanded one-by-one.)[^31^]

## Abstract

Background/Objectives: Lutathera® ([177Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE) is the first radiolabelled somatostatin (SST) analog approved for the treatment of patients with well-differentiated (G1 and G2) unresectable or metastatic gastro-entero-pancreatic neuro-endocrine-neoplasms (GEP-NENs). The bone marrow and kidneys are critical organs for RLT with [177Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE. Our purpose was to evaluate hematological and renal toxicity in 29 patients (18 males, 11 females) treated with Lutathera®. Methods: According to standard protocols, four cycles of (177Lu)Lu-DOTA-TATE were administered every eight/nine weeks. Patients received pre-medication with anti-emetic and anti-acid drugs and a slow amino acid infusion for renal protection. Blood count and serum creatinine data were collected at three time points: before the first cycle, after the second cycle, and at the end of treatment. Results: We found that almost all hematological parameters significantly decreased between the baseline and/or interim and post-therapy evaluation, although without a clinical impact. The presence of total tumor load or bone metastases had no influence on these findings, while male patients showed less hematological toxicity than females. Conversely, creatinine levels did not vary during treatment. Conclusions: Our study confirms that [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE RLT is safe and well tolerated despite some minor (grade 1) hematological toxicity.

## 1. Introduction

Neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) belong to a group of tumors originating from neuroendocrine cells that are distributed throughout the human body. Approximately two-thirds of NENs are derived from the gastrointestinal system and represent a group of gastro-enteropancreatic tumors (GEP-NENs). Over the last few years, more classifications of GEP-NENs have been introduced to identify reproducible criteria for diagnosis and prognostic significance; however, all these classifications have in common the identification of two NENs families: well-differentiated NENs and poorly differentiated NENs [1]. NENs have a variable high expression level of somatostatin receptors (SSTRs), and most of them are eligible for tumor imaging and therapy with radiolabelled somatostatin (SST) analogs [2].

web_context.title: Safety of Peptide Receptor Radionuclide Therapy with 177Lu-DOTATATE in NET patients with chronic kidney disease
